It does NOT deliver this cap's acceptance, for TWO independently measured reasons. (1) OBSERVABILITY: only P-037 has an observable surface (`metric.report.render_ms`, `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs:561`). P-025 / P-027 / P-045 have no `metric.*` target on the Pulse side -- the full 18-target inventory contains no halo, constellation, discovery or counter-refresh measure, and the entire frontend bridge is one procedure, `telemetry.frontend.record_frame_ms` (`crates/ui-bridge/src/telemetry.rs:99`) -- and no latency assertion on the harness side either (`halo-hue-encoding.toml:27` grades the hue by operator observation; `findings-counter-refresh.toml:10-11` calls the <=1s timing an unbuilt Epoch-8 measurement with 'no content token for the latency'; `slo_tier` is a coarse scenario-duration envelope, not a per-cap latency assertion). Asserting the other three requires BUILDING three observables, each a full TauRPC quadruple binding + allowlist leaf + an a11y-gated webview change. (2) HARNESS PREMISE: the storm scenario's single-fingerprint premise no longer holds at HEAD -- and the failure shape is in its ASSERTIONS, not in storm formation. `scenarios/fingerprint-storm.toml:9-13` encodes the superseded pre-token-leading normalization; its `variants = [identical, path, line]` triple over 18 occurrences SPLITS into two fingerprints, because the line variant is unaffected (the `:line` suffix drops regardless) while the path variant stays RELATIVE (`conductor-emit/src/exception.rs:414-421`) and so separates under token-leading.
